correctness.rationale: For every prime p congruent 3 modulo 8, quadratic reciprocity ensures a nonzero a with a^2=-2. Four explicit nonzero Fourier coefficients cancel at all four support points. For all p congruent 3 modulo 4 the quadratic form Q(x,y)=x^2+y^2 is anisotropic, so principal minors of sizes one and two are nonsingular. For three points the determinant factorization into root-of-unity differences and the strictly positive sine-phase comparison imply A=B=C, hence an impossible nonzero isotropic difference. All cases, quantifiers, normalization, and nonvanishing coefficients are covered. The exact finite verifier is corroborative only.

originality.rationale: The motivating 2026 paper (arXiv:2608.06335, Proposition 3) explicitly regards the minimum self-disjoint support in the p congruent 3 modulo 4 plane case as unresolved, exhibiting only support 2p-2. The four-point construction and matching three-point obstruction settle a natural infinite subfamily p congruent 3 modulo 8. The closest fully read Kronecker Fourier paper computes Hamming-number bounds without forcing the rows and columns of a rank-deficient submatrix to coincide. The inspected three-sparse exact-spectrum and cyclic principal-minor results do not determine this four-point self-disjoint minimum. Unindexed equivalent constructions remain a nonzero bibliographic risk.
residual_risks: An older or unindexed principal Fourier minor construction for the same F_p^2 pairing might imply the four-point witness; no global priority claim is made.
The full text of some secondary cyclic-principal-minor papers was not inspected; these concern cyclic character tables and are lower-likelihood comparators.
Nothing is claimed for the p congruent 7 modulo 8 family or other bilinear pairings.

value.rationale: Exact minimal self-disjoint Fourier support is a concrete question singled out in Zhou's recent study. This theorem reduces the best supplied 2p-2 witness to the sharp constant four for infinitely many primes (strictly from p=11 on) and proves an obstruction for all smaller support sizes. The congruence-class square-root mechanism is structural and pertinent to principal Fourier rank defects; the result is neither a renaming nor an arbitrary numerical case.
